exposure: Maternal hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) status
Mode of birth (vaginal delivery vs. Cesarean section)
outcome: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of hepatitis B virus (HBV)
cohort: The study enrolled 256 mother-child pairs with positive maternal hepatitis B surface antigens (HBsAg), whose children received passive-active immunization after birth.
finding: A high maternal HBV DNA level and vaginal delivery were identified as significant risk factors for HBV immunoprophylaxis failure, leading to mother-to-child transmission of HBV.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was identified as a risk factor for HBV immunoprophylaxis failure (OR=6.96, 95% CI, 1.80-26.93, p=0.005).
